alex: quick sync — ran the 6h stress profile on staging last night. p95 looks fine (~115ms) but p99 has large tail spikes when KV miss rate climbs above ~8%. profiler shows lots of kernel handoffs and very small effective batch sizes under sustained qps. thinking about a dynamic admission/drop policy to protect p99 by shedding low-priority work when gpu queue_len > 40. thoughts?

maria: can you paste the profiler snippet and the batch distribution?
alex: pasted below (truncated):
```
# sample profiler output
time_window=60s
avg_batch_size=3.1
batch_size_p50=2
batch_size_p95=6
kernel_switches=124
kernel: flash_attn_v2 avg_ms=1.1
fallback: matmul_fused avg_ms=2.8 switch_count=46
kv_cache_miss_rate=9.4%
p95_latency=115ms p99_latency=540ms (during spike)
queue_len_samples: [12,28,41,55,62,48,30]
```
jun: how do you plan to mark "low-priority"? we need a deterministic rule for fairness.
alex: proposal: two heuristics (can run together):
- quickreject: if request.has_embedding==true OR token_len < 20 and not enterprise_tier -> candidate for drop/queue timeout
- sampler: if suffix_cache_hit==false and kv_miss_rate_high -> probabilistic drop (start at 5%)
sam: worried about app-level correctness. dropping embeddings might break product. maybe prefer delaying noninteractive calls (batch window 250ms) over outright drop. also debounce the admission decisions for 10s windows.
ops-bot: deploy started: runtime/drop-policy/v0.1 -> canary to 10% of staging GPUs
maria: also a kernel angle — the profiler shows frequent kernel selection churn. if we keep avg_seq_len buckets and pin preferred kernel per-bucket we can avoid extra selection cost. small batches amplify handoff overhead. maybe increase batch aggregation window slightly when queue_len>threshold rather than immediate dropping.
sre: i'd set target_gpu_util = 0.72 (72%) for these experiments. above that leverage soft shedding + 200ms queue_timeout. hard shed only when queue_len > 75 or p99>600ms for >30s. also suggest circuit-breaker counter for any customer that sees >3% errors.
alex: good — proposed plan: A/B test 3 arms on staging: 
A) baseline
B) soft-shed + batch-window increase (250ms) + kernel-pin by seq_bucket
C) probabilistic drop (5%) on low-priority + hard-shed threshold 75
Metrics: p95/p99, tokens/s, successful_requests%, perceived_error_rate
I'll run 2h runs and post results. starting canary now. @maria @jun pls review drop rule edge cases.
maria: also add a small KV-prefetch experiment: prefetch top_k=3 for repeated prefixes — reduced miss_rate by ~2% in local run. worth A/Bing.
jun: for fairness testing add synthetic mix that nails long-seq chat + short-embed combos.
alex: ack. kicking off. will share perf artifacts and flamegraphs. :rocket:
